title: CAMEL/TCAP: Always compute SRT data
description: Rather than share globals with taps, always compute the stats needed for CAMEL/TCAP dissector

notes.body:
@AndersBroman - The stats don't seem that "processor intensive", but your name is at least on the dissector (from many years ago).  Do you have an opinion on this?
I'm just looking to remove the global variable dependency this creates outside of dissector code.
Sorry no. I did not do the SRT stat.

I looked at this a little bit recently. The globals are definitely ugly. I think the current implementation manages to conserve memory on one-pass TShark in a way that virtually no other code does. Which is sort of nice (there's lots of places in the code where if we know we're in TShark we could free file scoped memory that we have to keep around for random access in Wireshark), but perhaps not worth the complications for a relatively small tap. A general API for that scenario would be nice, though.
Are you suggesting a "are we tapping right now" API to replace the checks the globals are doing?

Maybe. The problem seems more general than just tapping. In this particular case, right now (and one thing that gets removed here) is that when it's tapped in TShark, once the call is closed and all its stats are added to the tap information, it gets removed from the map. I think the idea was to free the memory used, so that if you run TShark on a very long file with many calls, the memory consumption doesn't keep increasing with this file scoped data that isn't needed anymore after the call closes.

There's probably a fair amount of request-response processing that isn't needed after the response is done, at least in one-pass TShark (but would be needed in Wireshark.) There's no real good way for a dissector to check if we're in one-pass TShark. Even if it could, that might be cumbersome to do. TShark has the `-M` flag to free all the memory, but something like a wmem scope that is periodically freed in one-pass TShark (but behaves like file scope in Wireshark) might be a way to make it easier for dissectors and taps.

The idea that I had (and I may hold off this MR because this code logic could be used as a test) is a new wmem scope that we can apply for tap and request/response data.  I think many times it will behave similar to file-scope, but the dissector shouldn't have to care about it.
The idea didn't really materialize, so submitting this MR to get rid of the globals.
My feeling is getting rid of the globals and ultimately using common CLI SRT tap code is worth the tradeoffs in memory and CPU cycles.
